summary: Too small crawls, too big blows up. There is a hard limit in between.
headline: The step size has a ceiling
overview: For a bowl-shaped loss, descent is stable only when the learning rate stays below 2 divided by the steepest curvature of the bowl. The widget works that number out for this data and marks it.
Below the limit the loss falls. Above it, every step overshoots by more than it fixed.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Press the button to jump just past the limit. The loss curve turns rose and climbs.

check.question: You double the learning rate and the loss starts growing. What is the likely cause?
options: The step now overshoots the minimum
The model has too few parameters

realLife: Training logs that suddenly show a loss of NaN usually mean a learning rate that was too high for that data.
data: Same sixteen points as the gradient descent lesson, so you can compare. Loss is drawn on a log scale so both slow and exploding runs fit on screen.
maths: Near the minimum the loss is a quadratic. Along each direction the error is multiplied by this each step, where λ is the curvature:
Stable when this holds for every λ:
The Google course shows 0.03 working and 1 failing on its data. Those numbers belong to that data, not to learning rates in general.
code:
lam_max = np.linalg.eigvalsh(2/n * Z.T @ Z)[-1]   # Z = [X, 1]
lr_limit = 2 / lam_max
